title: Kinetic and Potential Energy
seo_title: Kinetic and Potential Energy Worksheets: ½mv², mgh, Work and Power (High School Physics)
standard_text: Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as a combination of energy associated with the motions of particles (objects) and energy associated with the relative position of particles (objects).
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on kinetic and potential energy (NGSS HS-PS3-2): KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, elastic energy, work and power. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: KE = ½mv², PE = mgh; work moves energy from one form or object to another.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is either motion (kinetic) or stored by position (potential).

  • KE = ½mv² (double the speed → 4 times the KE). Gravitational PE = mgh. Elastic PE = ½kx².
  • Work W = Fd transfers energy; power P = W ÷ t.
  • At the particle level, thermal energy is particle motion; chemical energy is stored in particle positions.
Example

KE of 2 kg at 3 m/s?

½ × 2 × 3²

Answer: 9 J

Example

PE of 10 kg lifted 2 m?

10 × 9.8 × 2

Answer: 196 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking doubling speed doubles kinetic energy.
  • Forgetting the ½ in ½mv².
  • Thinking work is done when nothing moves.

faq.q: How do you calculate kinetic energy?
faq.a: KE = ½mv². Because speed is squared, doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy four times larger.

faq.q: How do you calculate gravitational potential energy?
What is the difference between work and power?
faq.a: Work is energy transferred by a force (W = Fd). Power is how fast the work is done (P = W ÷ t).
